layout_dets.text: The results discussed in Chapter 4 are obviously applicable to linear trans-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: formations mapping one unitary space into another. Some additional

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: properties of transformations resulting from the existence of the inner

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: product are considered in this chapter. In particular, it will be shown that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: any linear transformation acting on a unitary space has a dual transforma-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion, known as its “adjoint." Normal matrices and transformations are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: defined and studied in terms of adjoints prior to the analysis of the important

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: subclasses of Hermitian matrices (and self-adjoint transformations) and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: unitary matrices and transformations. All of these special classes are subsets

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the simple matrices and transformations introduced in Chapter 4.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for example, projectors and the reduction of quadratic forms. The chapter

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
